description: An extends clause names the parent of a subclass that declares its own constructor
code:
class Animal(name):
    this.name = name
class Dog(name, breed) extends Animal:
    this.name = name
    this.breed = breed
rex = Dog("Rex", "lab")
[rex.name, rex.breed, Dog.length, Animal.length]

description: A bodyless extends header declares a subclass that uses its parent's constructor
code:
class Point(x, y):
    this.x = x
    this.y = y
class Pixel extends Point
p = Pixel(3, 4)
[p.x, p.y, Pixel.length, Point.length]

description: Class-level rules of the parent stay live on instances of an extends subclass
code:
class Employee(name, salary):
    this.name = name
    this.salary = salary
$Employee.senior = $Employee.salary > 5000
class Manager extends Employee
ana = Manager("ana", 4000)
bo = Manager("bo", 7000)
ana.salary = 6000
[ana.senior, bo.senior, Employee.length]

description: An init method in an extends subclass forwards its parent's arguments with super
Bare super runs every constructor of an extends chain on the same instance
The colon and extends spellings of a subclass declare the same kind of class
code:
class Shape(sides):
    this.sides = sides
class Square: Shape
    pass
class Cube extends Shape
a = Square(4)
b = Cube(4)
[a.sides == b.sides, Square.length, Cube.length, Shape.length]

description: extends stays an ordinary name for variables, properties and parameters
code:
extends = 5
settings = {extends: 2}
def grow(extends) => extends + 1
[extends * settings.extends, grow(extends)]

description: An extends clause that would close an inheritance cycle raises a TypeError
code:
class Root
class Branch extends Root
failure = ""
try:
    class Root extends Branch
catch error:
    failure = error
failure
